This is the private Polars data plane. Public build/serve, runtime dispatch, input/output expectation evaluation and publication composition remain T061–T067; other transform adapters remain later tasks.
Caller holds runtime ownership, input leases and resource policy, verifies environment and completes required input expectations before execution.
The worker manifest is evidence only. Rust returns a closed invisible candidate; no worker or adapter updates catalogue heads.
Polars physical fields are nullable; explicit schemas must match exactly. Unsupported schema types and submicrosecond Python datetime parameters fail rather than silently coerce.
Context secret delivery requires the later source service. Process-group cancellation and heartbeat disconnect use the existing supervisor; no hostile-code sandbox is claimed.
Streaming measurement concerns the worker and this query shape. Eager user code, joins/sorts/UDFs and Rust artifact validation have separate resource costs.
No dependency pins, public CLI envelope, runtime schema 7, protocol 1.0 or specification 1.1.2 version changes.
